title: Check yourself: Skills, and how they compare with the other ways to extend Claude Code

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A description reads only "Release helper", and Claude never loads that skill when users ask for a changelog. What is the first fix?

options.text: Raise the tool grant so that the skill may run any shell command
options.says: Ruled out because a tool grant is for "Tools Claude may use without asking while the skill runs", and a skill that is never loaded never runs.

options.text: State what it does and when to use it, in everyday words
options.says: The page says the description is "What the skill does and when to use it. Claude uses this to decide when to apply the skill."

options.text: Move the folder into the enterprise location so it takes priority
options.says: Ruled out because location decides which skill wins when "two skills share a name", and has no bearing on whether Claude matches a request.

options.text: Add the value true on the model-invocation field in the frontmatter
options.says: Ruled out because the table says `true` "stops Claude from starting it by itself", which is the opposite of what the team wants.

questions.stem: A team needs to guarantee that no agent pushes to the main branch, whatever Claude decides in a given turn. Which extension fits best?

options.text: A memory line, which loads as persistent context in each conversation
options.says: Ruled out because the table calls it "Persistent context loaded every conversation" for conventions, which is guidance Claude may still get wrong, and the page says a rule that must never be broken needs a hook or a deny rule.

options.text: A skill, which holds instructions that Claude may follow
options.says: Ruled out because "a skill is instructions Claude may follow", and an instruction that may be followed is not a guarantee.

options.text: A hook, which runs as a program on every matching event
options.says: The page says "A rule that must never be broken belongs in a hook or a deny rule", and a hook is "a program that always runs".

options.text: A subagent, which is an isolated context returning summaries
options.says: Ruled out because a subagent is "An isolated context that returns summarised results" for "A side task that would flood the conversation", and not a gate that every command must pass.

questions.stem: A skill tags a release and creates a GitHub release. Which frontmatter is right?

options.text: Automatic invocation off, with two command patterns pre-approved
options.says: The page says a task skill with side effects should set `disable-model-invocation: true`, and that `allowed-tools: Bash(git tag *) Bash(gh release create *)` "approves two command families".

options.text: Automatic invocation on, with the whole Bash tool pre-approved
options.says: Ruled out because the page says bare `Bash` "approves every shell command for that turn".

options.text: Automatic invocation on, with the two command patterns pre-approved
options.says: Ruled out because "a person should start it" when a skill has side effects.

options.text: Automatic invocation off, with the whole Bash tool pre-approved
options.says: Ruled out because it keeps the person in control but the page says bare `Bash` "turns a narrow skill into an open one".
